chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from al-Sakuni from Ja'far from his father from his forefathers from Ali (peace be upon him)

That he ruled between two men who claimed a she-camel, so one of them presented two witnesses and the other five, and he said, 'For the owner of the five witnesses is five shares, and for the owner of the two witnesses is two shares.'
ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence determine the division of a disputed asset when parties present unequal numbers of witnesses?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him), recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the principle of proportional distribution based on witness count is applied to a dispute over a she-camel. This precedent highlights the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in evidentiary matters, where the weight of testimony can determine the division of rights rather than a binary win/lose outcome. It serves as a foundational example for resolving conflicting claims in commercial and property disputes within the Imami tradition.
